**Museum, exhibit, and room that house the “Mona Lisa of prehistory” mask (the Mask of Agamemnon)**  

| Category | Details | Source |
|----------|---------|--------|
| Museum | National Archaeological Museum, Athens, Greece | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mask_of_Agamemnon |
| Exhibit / Collection | Mycenaean Antiquities (part of the museum’s Pre‑historic Collection) | Same Wikipedia entry; Greece Is article notes it is “mounted centrally with the other gold masks from Grave Circle A, amid the spectacular Collection of Mycenaean Antiquities.” |
| Room | Room 4 | https://www.greece-is.com/archaeological-treasures-in-greece-the-mask-of-agamemnon/ |

**Notes**

* The mask is indeed described as the “Mona Lisa of prehistory” and is displayed in the National Archaeological Museum of Athens.  
* While the museum’s Pre‑historic Collection is spread across rooms 3‑6 and 48, the specific Mycenaean Antiquities exhibit containing the mask is located in Room 4.  
* The exhibit’s formal title can be referenced as “Mycenaean Antiquities” or as part of the broader Pre‑historic Collection—both descriptions are used in the cited sources.
